/-!
# Conjecture 8.29

by L. A. Kurdachenko

Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. A group
satisfies the *weak maximal condition for normal subgroups* (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if it has no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite.
Equivalently, in every ascending chain of normal subgroups all but finitely many of the
indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ are finite. This is weaker than the maximal condition for normal
subgroups $\mathrm{Max}\text{-}n$ (the ascending chain condition on normal subgroups).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)` / ACC-style conditions (these give ordinary Max-n, which the notes explicitly say is NOT the intended condition); `Subgroup.IsFiniteRelIndex` (used implicitly via `relIndex = 0`).
justification.name: Kourovka.«8.29».WeakMaxNormal
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no weak maximal condition (Baer's Max-∞-n). Defined as: there is no `N : ℕ → Subgroup G` with all `N i` normal, `StrictMono N`, and `(N i).relIndex (N (i+1)) = 0` for all `i` (i.e. every index |N_{i+1} : N_i| infinite; `Subgroup.relIndex` returns 0 exactly for infinite index, and since `N i ≤ N (i+1)` the relative index is exactly |N_{i+1} : N_i|).

blocks.name: WeakMaxNormal
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if there is no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups of `G` in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$
is infinite.

Here `(N i).relIndex (N (i + 1))` is the index of `N i` in `N (i + 1)`, and `Subgroup.relIndex`
returns `0` exactly when this index is infinite. -/
def WeakMaxNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → Subgroup G,
    (∀ i, (N i).Normal) ∧ StrictMono N ∧ ∀ i, (N i).relIndex (N (i + 1)) = 0

blocks.docstring:
Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

That is: is there a nontrivial group $G$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent, $Z(G) = 1$, and $G$ has no infinite strictly ascending chain $N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$
of normal subgroups with all indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ infinite?

The trivial group satisfies all three conditions vacuously, so it is excluded by `Nontrivial G`.

-/

theorem kourovka.«8.29» : answer(sorry) ↔

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no existence question: the Prop is ∃ a nontrivial group G that is locally nilpotent (every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent), has Subgroup.center G = ⊥, and satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups (Baer's Max-∞-n: there is no infinite strictly ascending chain N₁ < N₂ < ⋯ of normal subgroups with every index |N_{i+1} : N_i| infinite, equivalently every ascending chain of normal subgroups has finite-index steps from some point on); the trivial group must be excluded explicitly since it vacuously satisfies all three conditions, and note that 'weak maximal' is not the ordinary Max-n (ACC on normal subgroups).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ nontrivial group G (in Type) that is locally nilpotent (every Subgroup.FG subgroup is Group.IsNilpotent), has Subgroup.center G = ⊥, and satisfies Baer's Max-∞-n. c01–c04, c06, c07 use the 'no strictly ascending ℕ-chain of G-normal subgroups with every consecutive relIndex = 0 (= infinite)' form; c05 and c08 use the equivalent 'every monotone chain of normal subgroups eventually has finite-index steps' form (equivalent by extracting the subsequence of infinite-index steps, using multiplicativity of index in towers). Mathlib's Subgroup.relIndex H K is |K : H ∩ K| and is 0 exactly when infinite, so with N i < N (i+1) it is exactly |N_{i+1} : N_i|. The final file uses c01's definitions and main theorem verbatim (StrictMono form, closest to 'N₁ < N₂ < ⋯'), adds c02's Max-n ⇒ weak Max-n API lemma and trivial-group test (documenting why Nontrivial G is required), and c01/c06's finite-group API lemma. Compiles with only the sorry warning.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 8.29

by L. A. Kurdachenko

Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

A group is *locally nilpotent* if every finitely generated subgroup is nilpotent. A group
satisfies the *weak maximal condition for normal subgroups* (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if it has no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ is infinite.
Equivalently, in every ascending chain of normal subgroups all but finitely many of the
indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ are finite. This is weaker than the maximal condition for normal
subgroups $\mathrm{Max}\text{-}n$ (the ascending chain condition on normal subgroups).

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«8.29»

/-- A group `G` is locally nilpotent if every finitely generated subgroup of `G` is nilpotent. -/
def IsLocallyNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ H : Subgroup G, H.FG → Group.IsNilpotent H

/-- A group `G` satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups (Baer's condition
$\mathrm{Max}\text{-}\infty\text{-}n$) if there is no infinite strictly ascending chain
$N_0 < N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ of normal subgroups of `G` in which every index $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$
is infinite.

Here `(N i).relIndex (N (i + 1))` is the index of `N i` in `N (i + 1)`, and `Subgroup.relIndex`
returns `0` exactly when this index is infinite. -/
def WeakMaxNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ N : ℕ → Subgroup G,
    (∀ i, (N i).Normal) ∧ StrictMono N ∧ ∀ i, (N i).relIndex (N (i + 1)) = 0

/-- A nilpotent group is locally nilpotent. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent (G : Type*) [Group G] [Group.IsNilpotent G] :
    IsLocallyNilpotent G :=
  fun _ _ => inferInstance

/-- A finite group satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMaxNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : WeakMaxNormal G :=
  fun ⟨_, _, _, h⟩ => Subgroup.index_ne_zero_of_finite (h 0)

/-- A group satisfying the maximal condition for normal subgroups (no infinite strictly
ascending chain of normal subgroups at all) satisfies the weak maximal condition for normal
subgroups. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem WeakMaxNormal.of_forall_not_strictMono (G : Type*) [Group G]
    (h : ∀ N : ℕ → Subgroup G, (∀ i, (N i).Normal) → ¬ StrictMono N) :
    WeakMaxNormal G :=
  fun ⟨N, hN, hlt, _⟩ => h N hN hlt

/-- The trivial group is a locally nilpotent group with trivial centre satisfying the weak
maximal condition for normal subgroups. This is why the problem asks for a nontrivial group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem trivial_group_satisfies_conditions :
    IsLocallyNilpotent Unit ∧ Subgroup.center Unit = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal Unit :=
  ⟨IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent Unit, Subsingleton.elim _ _, WeakMaxNormal.of_finite Unit⟩

/--
Do there exist locally nilpotent groups with trivial centre satisfying the weak maximal
condition for normal subgroups?

That is: is there a nontrivial group $G$ such that every finitely generated subgroup of $G$ is
nilpotent, $Z(G) = 1$, and $G$ has no infinite strictly ascending chain $N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$
of normal subgroups with all indices $|N_{i+1} : N_i|$ infinite?

The trivial group satisfies all three conditions vacuously, so it is excluded by `Nontrivial G`.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«8.29» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G), Nontrivial G ∧ IsLocallyNilpotent G ∧
      Subgroup.center G = ⊥ ∧ WeakMaxNormal G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«8.29»

items: Weak maximal condition formalized in the 'no bad chain' form (no strictly ascending ℕ-indexed chain of normal subgroups with every consecutive index infinite), which is Baer's/Robinson's literal definition; the equivalent 'eventually finite-index steps' form is mentioned in the module docstring but not used.

`StrictMono N` is included for literal faithfulness to 'N₁ < N₂ < ⋯'; it is in fact implied by the infinite-index condition (equal consecutive terms would have relIndex 1, not 0), so it is harmless redundancy.
Infinite index is expressed as `Subgroup.relIndex … = 0`, relying on Mathlib's convention that `relIndex` returns 0 exactly for infinite index; this is documented in the definition's docstring.
The group is quantified over `Type` (universe 0), following the existing Kourovka files (e.g. 1_74.lean).
`Nontrivial G` is added to exclude the trivial group, which would otherwise make the existential trivially true; this is explained in the theorem docstring.

Two short fully-proved `@[category API]` tests (`IsLocallyNilpotent.of_isNilpotent`, `WeakMaxNormal.of_finite`) are included to exercise the bespoke definitions, per the repository's 'add basic API tests' guideline; the bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean) since the task restricts writing to the candidate file.

reviewer_notes: The problem is a single yes/no existence question; the trivial group vacuously satisfies all three conditions, so Nontrivial G is imposed (per decomposition table; every candidate did this). No further finiteness hypothesis is needed: any witness is automatically infinite and non-nilpotent, since a nontrivial nilpotent group has nontrivial centre. 'Weak maximal condition for normal subgroups' is taken as Baer/Zaitsev Max-∞-n (no infinite strictly ascending chain of normal subgroups with all indices |N_{i+1}:N_i| infinite), which is Kurdachenko's own usage in his 1980s papers on this condition; it is deliberately not the ordinary Max-n. Chains are ℕ-indexed, as in the literature definition. Normality is normality in the ambient group G. Bespoke definitions IsLocallyNilpotent and WeakMaxNormal are kept in the problem file (as in Kourovka/1_40.lean and 1_74.lean) because the output is a single file; a maintainer may wish to move IsLocallyNilpotent to FormalConjecturesForMathlib. No candidate omitted the slot and no omission reasons needed weighing. Minor differences among candidates (StrictMono vs ∀ i, N i < N (i+1); Nontrivial as ∧-conjunct vs existential instance; named defs vs inline) are purely stylistic and all equivalent.
